Methods for ordinal models with threshold-specific slopes

Source: R/ordinal-partial-methods.R
ordinal-partial-methods.Rd

Partial proportional-odds models allow selected predictor effects to differ across cumulative thresholds. The same parameter layout is available for probit and complementary log-log links, with interpretation on their link scales. Common slopes and threshold-specific slopes are displayed separately.

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_ordinal_partial'
coef(
  object,
  component = c("all", "location", "threshold", "common", "nonparallel"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_ordinal_partial'
vcov(
  object,
  component = c("all", "location", "threshold", "common", "nonparallel"),
  type = c("model", "HC0", "HC1"),
  cluster = NULL,
  cadjust = TRUE,
  block.size = 8192L,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_ordinal_partial'
summary(object, vcov. = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.fastglm_ordinal_partial'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_ordinal_partial'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_ordinal_partial'
confint(
  object,
  parm,
  level = 0.95,
  method = c("wald", "profile"),
  control = list(),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_ordinal_partial'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("probability", "cumulative", "class", "link", "response"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  offset = NULL,
  ...
)

tidy.fastglm_ordinal_partial(
  x,
  conf.int = FALSE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  component = c("all", "location", "threshold", "common", "nonparallel"),
  vcov. = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object, x

a fitted fastglm_ordinal_partial model, or its summary.

component

coefficient block: "all", "location" (all slopes), "threshold", "common", or "nonparallel".

...

further method arguments.

type

for vcov(), "model" for inverse expected information, or "HC0" or "HC1" for ordinary-score sandwich covariance. All thresholds and both slope blocks enter the joint observed-information calculation. For predict(), the scale: "probability" (or "response"), "cumulative", "class", or "link". Nonparallel link predictions are an observation-by-threshold matrix of cumulative predictors alpha[j] - x_common beta - x_nonparallel gamma[,j] - offset. Applying the inverse link gives the cumulative probabilities.

cluster, cadjust, block.size

cluster identifiers, cluster adjustment, and processing block size, as in fastglm_vcov(). Supplying cluster requires type="HC0" or type="HC1". For mean-bias-reduced fits, sandwich covariance uses the same first-order ordinary-score convention and regularity assumptions described there. For a source fit, cluster is a function of block index returning identifiers in original block row order. Repeated identifiers may span source blocks.

vcov.

optional full coefficient covariance for a converged fit.

digits

number of significant digits used for display.

parm

parameters by name or position; defaults to all parameters.

level

confidence level.

method

interval method: "wald" or, for maximum-likelihood fits with retained data, "profile".

control

numerical controls for profile fitting, as described in fastglm_score_test().

newdata

prediction data, as in predict.fastglm_ordinal().

se.fit

include full-model delta-method standard errors.

offset

optional replacement location offset.

conf.int

include Wald confidence limits in broom::tidy() output.

conf.level

confidence level for broom::tidy().

exponentiate

exponentiate slopes and their confidence limits. Odds-ratio interpretation applies to the logit link, with separate ratios for each threshold when a predictor has a nonparallel effect.

Value

Coefficients, covariance, predictions, or a summary as appropriate. Printing invisibly returns the supplied object.

Details

The coefficient vector contains thresholds, common slopes, and threshold-specific slopes, in that order. Within the last block, all selected predictors for the first threshold precede those for the second threshold. object$gamma also stores these slopes as a predictor-by-threshold matrix. Selecting component="location" includes both kinds of slope.

Thresholds describe the cumulative predictors when the covariates and offset equal zero. That covariate combination can lie outside the valid prediction domain, so the reported thresholds need not be ordered in isolation. The cumulative predictors are constrained to be ordered at positive-frequency training rows and checked again at prediction rows. Invalid predictions report the affected rows. Probability clipping or threshold reordering is not used to repair an invalid prediction.

Model-based covariance is inverse expected Fisher information, including covariance between all thresholds and slopes. Wald intervals and delta-method prediction standard errors are first-order approximations under an interior correctly specified model with independent observations or integer frequency counts and nonsingular limiting information. Numerical convergence alone does not establish those assumptions. With firth=TRUE, the full-model cumulative-link adjustment targets the leading mean bias of the reported thresholds, common slopes, and threshold-specific slopes. These adjusted equations do not generally maximize a scalar penalized likelihood. Empty-category reductions require additional parameter constraints and are not supported for these fits.
